stories.title: S. Korea employs helicopters for 2nd day to search for 9 missing nationals following massive flood
stories.summary: SEOUL, Aug. 30 (Yonhap) -- The government plans to continue using helicopters in...
article_sentences: The government plans to continue using helicopters in search operations Sunday in Nepal to locate nine South Koreans who have gone missing after a catastrophic flash flood devastated the Himalayan country, the foreign ministry said.
Two helicopters are scheduled to be used: one chartered by the government's rapid response team and the other chartered by Doosan Enerbility.
Flight authorization has yet to be granted, however, as ground conditions and decisions by Nepali authorities overseeing the rescue effort remain fluid.

On Saturday, a government-charted helicopter carrying four rapid response team members flew twice from Kathmandu toward the flood site, becoming reportedly the only non-Nepali aircraft cleared to fly that day.
The helicopter reportedly failed to land, and the search was instead conducted visually, with footage from the flight analyzed.
Six employees of Doosan Enerbility Co.
and three of Korea South-East Power Co.
remain missing since the massive floods struck Nepal's north-central Himalayan border area Wednesday.
They had been working at a hydroelectric power plant construction site in the Rasuwa district when the floods hit the region.
Ten other Doosan workers who had been isolated at a different location have been moved to safety.
A ministry official said Sunday's search area would be larger than the previous day's.

stories.title: Thailand proposes $17 (450-baht) fee to fund tourism upgrade
stories.summary: Collection would begin with travellers arriving by air.
article_sentences: Thailand plans to charge a 450-baht ($17) fee to foreign visitors to fund tourism infrastructure, insurance, environmental restoration and workforce development.
The fee aims to shift the industry towards higher-quality and sustainable tourism, reducing reliance on limited state budgets.
The proposal includes off-budget fund management with calls for transparency and industry involvement; Cabinet approval is pending after public consultation.

Thailand is reviving its proposed 450-baht ($17) fee on foreign visitors as a long-term source of funding for insurance, destination renewal and a shift towards higher-quality tourism, with officials warning that continued dependence on increasingly limited state budgets could leave the industry at risk of stagnation.

Revenue would be channelled into the Tourism Promotion Fund to support tourist attractions and infrastructure, environmental restoration, research, workforce development, tourism promotion and assistance for local communities.
The fund would also finance insurance and health protection for foreign visitors.
The Association of Thai Travel Agents (ATTA) has estimated that the fee could generate about 10 billion baht in off-budget revenue for the tourism industry.
Tourism and Sports Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul said the prevailing view was that Thailand needed a dedicated fund to finance improvements across the sector.
“The figures clearly show that, without such a fund, Thailand’s tourism industry is approaching saturation or could begin to decline,” he said.
“Relying on a state budget that becomes more limited each year would create greater constraints on competitiveness.
The government therefore intends to secure off-budget funding to drive and upgrade tourism in every area.”
The government wants to move Thailand’s tourism industry towards a higher-value and more sustainable model, rather than relying primarily on continued growth in visitor numbers.

stories.title: Fire-walking during Aadi festivals: How to escape burns?Health Wrap | Episode 48
stories.summary: Aadi, the Tamil month associated with several temple festivals and religious observances, sees many devotees taking part in practices such as fire-walking and prolonged barefoot walking. Exposure to extreme heat can cause burns, blisters and other injuries to the feet. In this episode of Health Wrap, Ramya Kannan, Health Editor, The Hindu, speaks to an expert about the risks of foot injuries during fire-walking, what people should watch out for after exposure to extreme heat and when an injury requires medical attention.
